\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{نجات} (najāt)}{نجات (najāt)}]{\ur{نجات} (najāt) — deliverance; release (from danger or trouble)}

\label{lesson:UR-C296-najat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to pull out, then the Urdu for in a sorry state.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{نجات}}
\textbf{\ur{نجات}} — \emph{najāt} — \textquotedblleft{}deliverance; release (from danger or trouble)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{صبح} \ur{تک} \ur{سب} \ur{کو} \ur{پانی} \ur{سے} \ur{نجات} \ur{ملی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{subah tak sab ko pānī se najāt milī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
By morning everyone had been delivered from the water.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{نجات}} (\emph{najāt}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{najāt}, \textquotedblleft{}deliverance, escape\textquotedblright{}. The one set free takes \textbf{\ur{کو}} and the danger takes \textbf{\ur{سے}}: \textbf{\ur{پانی} \ur{سے} \ur{نجات} \ur{ملی}}. It is feminine.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{najāt}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{najāt}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{subah tak sab ko pānī se najāt milī.} — By morning everyone had been delivered from the water.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to pull out, then the Urdu for in a sorry state, then say \emph{najāt} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{نجات} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Deliverance; release (from danger or trouble)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ہیلی} \ur{کاپٹر} (helī kāpṭar)}{ہیلی کاپٹر (helī kāpṭar)}]{\ur{ہیلی} \ur{کاپٹر} (helī kāpṭar) — a helicopter}

\label{lesson:UR-C296-heli-kaptar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for in a sorry state, then the Urdu for deliverance.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ہیلی} \ur{کاپٹر}}
\textbf{\ur{ہیلی} \ur{کاپٹر}} — \emph{helī kāpṭar} — \textquotedblleft{}a helicopter\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ہیلی} \ur{کاپٹر} \ur{نے} \ur{لوگوں} \ur{کو} \ur{بچایا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{helī kāpṭar ne logoṅ ko bachāyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The helicopter rescued people.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ہیلی} \ur{کاپٹر}} (\emph{helī kāpṭar}) is borrowed from English \emph{helicopter}. Urdu writes it as two words.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{helī kāpṭar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{helī kāpṭar ne logoṅ ko bachāyā.} — The helicopter rescued people.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for in a sorry state, then the Urdu for deliverance, then say \emph{helī kāpṭar} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{چھڑانا} (chhuṛānā)}{چھڑانا (chhuṛānā)}]{\ur{چھڑانا} (chhuṛānā) — to set free; to pull free}

\label{lesson:UR-C296-chhurana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for deliverance, then the Urdu for a helicopter.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{چھڑانا}}
\textbf{\ur{چھڑانا}} — \emph{chhuṛānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to set free; to pull free\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{رسی} \ur{سے} \ur{اپنا} \ur{ہاتھ} \ur{چھڑایا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{us ne rassī se apnā hāth chhuṛāyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He freed his hand from the rope.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{بکری} \ur{چھڑائی}, \emph{us ne bakrī chhuṛāī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{چھڑانا}} (\emph{chhuṛānā}) is usually taken as the causing partner of \textbf{\ur{چھوٹنا}}, to come loose, whose Hindi cousin \emph{chūṭnā}, \textquotedblleft{}escapes\textquotedblright{}, CDIAL lists under \emph{*kṣuṭyatē}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 3707): to make a thing come loose. What it is freed from takes \textbf{\ur{سے}}: \textbf{\ur{رسی} \ur{سے} \ur{ہاتھ} \ur{چھڑایا}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chhuṛānā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chhuṛānā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{us ne rassī se apnā hāth chhuṛāyā.} — He freed his hand from the rope.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for deliverance, then the Urdu for a helicopter, then say \emph{chhuṛānā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{لپکنا} (lapaknā)}{لپکنا (lapaknā)}]{\ur{لپکنا} (lapaknā) — to dart; to spring forward}

\label{lesson:UR-C296-lapakna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a helicopter, then the Urdu for to set free.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{لپکنا}}
\textbf{\ur{لپکنا}} — \emph{lapaknā} — \textquotedblleft{}to dart; to spring forward\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{وہ} \ur{پانی} \ur{کی} \ur{طرف} \ur{لپکا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{voh pānī kī taraf lapkā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He darted towards the water.
\end{quote}

Past (she …): \ur{وہ} \ur{لپکی}, \emph{voh lapkī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{لپکنا}} (\emph{lapaknā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{lapaknā}, \textquotedblleft{}to leap up\textquotedblright{}, under a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 10939).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{سلامت} (salāmat)}{سلامت (salāmat)}]{\ur{سلامت} (salāmat) — safe and sound}

\label{lesson:UR-C296-salamat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to set free, then the Urdu for to dart.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{سلامت}}
\textbf{\ur{سلامت}} — \emph{salāmat} — \textquotedblleft{}safe and sound\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{صبح} \ur{تک} \ur{سب} \ur{سلامت} \ur{تھے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{subah tak sab salāmat the.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
By morning everyone was safe and sound.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{سلامت}} (\emph{salāmat}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{salāma}, \textquotedblleft{}safety, soundness\textquotedblright{}, a cousin of \textbf{\ur{سلام}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
